q: How many unicorns do we have in total?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM unicorns
hint: Return one number.

q: List the unicorns that are currently available to rent.
sql: SELECT unicorn_name FROM current_unicorn_availability WHERE status = 'available' ORDER BY unicorn_name
hint: Return the unicorn names only.

q: What was our total revenue each month?
sql: SELECT year_month, total_revenue FROM monthly_revenue_summary ORDER BY year_month
hint: Return year-month and total revenue for every month.

q: Which unicorn breed earns the most revenue?
sql: SELECT breed FROM top_revenue_unicorn_breeds ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Return the breed name only.

q: Who are our top 5 customers by revenue?
sql: SELECT customer_name, total_revenue FROM top_revenue_customers ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5
hint: Return customer name and total revenue, 5 rows.

q: Which unicorns are due for maintenance in the next week?
sql: SELECT unicorn_name, days_until_due FROM unicorns_due_for_maintenance WHERE days_until_due <= 7 ORDER BY days_until_due
hint: Return unicorn name and days until due for every unicorn due within 7 days or already overdue.

q: How many bookings started on 15 December 2025?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bookings WHERE start_datetime::date = '2025-12-15'
hint: Return one number.

q: Which day of the week brings in the most revenue?
sql: SELECT day_name FROM revenue_by_time_and_day GROUP BY day_name ORDER BY SUM(total_revenue) DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Return the day name only, 1 row.

q: What subscription plan is my account on and how much does it cost per month?
sql: SELECT plan_name, monthly_price FROM account_subscription_status
hint: Return plan name and monthly price for each account.

q: How many customers are organizations versus individuals?
sql: SELECT customer_type, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY customer_type ORDER BY customer_type
hint: Return customer type and count.

q: What is the average hourly rate of our unicorns?
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(hourly_rate), 2) FROM unicorns
hint: Return one number rounded to 2 decimals.

q: Which unicorns have the lowest revenue?
sql: SELECT entity_name, total_revenue FROM bottom_revenue_unicorns ORDER BY total_revenue ASC LIMIT 5
hint: Return unicorn name and total revenue for the 5 lowest.

q: Which months are our busiest across the year?
sql: SELECT month_name FROM seasonal_trends GROUP BY month_number, month_name ORDER BY SUM(total_bookings) DESC LIMIT 3
hint: Return the month names of the 3 busiest months by bookings.

q: Which staff member generated the most booking revenue?
sql: SELECT staff_name, SUM(total_revenue_generated) r FROM staff_performance_metrics GROUP BY staff_name ORDER BY r DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Use booking total cost. Return the staff member's full name and the revenue, 1 row.

q: What is our total completed booking-fee amount?
sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'booking_fee' AND status = 'completed'
hint: Return one number.

q: What is the utilization rate of each unicorn?
sql: SELECT unicorn_name, utilization_rate FROM unicorn_utilization_rates ORDER BY utilization_rate DESC
hint: Return unicorn name and utilization rate for every unicorn.

q: Which customers are at risk of churning?
sql: SELECT customer_name, days_since_last_booking FROM customer_retention_metrics WHERE is_at_risk ORDER BY days_since_last_booking DESC
hint: Return customer name and days since last booking for every at-risk customer.

q: What is each customer's lifetime value?
sql: SELECT customer_name, total_revenue FROM customer_lifetime_value ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
hint: Return customer name and lifetime revenue for every customer.

q: How did revenue on 15 December 2025 compare with the same day the week before?
sql: SELECT account_id, revenue, same_day_last_week_revenue FROM revenue_comparison WHERE revenue_date = '2025-12-15' ORDER BY account_id
hint: Return account id, revenue and the same-day-last-week revenue, one row per account.

q: How many users does each role have?
sql: SELECT role, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY role ORDER BY role
hint: Return role and number of users.

q: List each customer with the number of bookings they have made.
sql: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(b.booking_id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN bookings b ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1
hint: Return customer id and booking count for every customer, including those with none.

q: What is the total booking cost per unicorn breed?
sql: SELECT u.breed, SUM(b.total_cost) FROM bookings b JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id GROUP BY u.breed ORDER BY 2 DESC
hint: Return breed and summed booking total cost.

q: Which unicorns have never been booked?
sql: SELECT u.name FROM unicorns u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bookings b WHERE b.unicorn_id = u.unicorn_id) ORDER BY u.name
hint: Return the unicorn names only.

q: Which unicorns had the most maintenance events in Q4 2025?
sql: SELECT u.name, COUNT(*) FROM unicorn_availability a JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = a.unicorn_id WHERE a.status = 'maintenance' AND a.created_at >= '2025-10-01' AND a.created_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY u.name ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1 LIMIT 10
hint: Return unicorn name and number of maintenance events for the top 10.

q: Which customers take the longest rides on average?
sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name, ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (b.end_datetime - b.start_datetime)) / 3600)::numeric, 1) FROM bookings b JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1 LIMIT 10
hint: Return customer full name and average ride hours for the top 10.

q: How many transactions do we have of each type and status?
sql: SELECT transaction_type, status, COUNT(*) FROM transactions GROUP BY 1, 2
hint: Return type, status and count.

q: Which staff members took bookings in December 2025 and how many each?
sql: SELECT u.first_name || ' ' || u.last_name, COUNT(*) FROM bookings b JOIN users u ON u.user_id = b.user_id WHERE b.start_datetime >= '2025-12-01' AND b.start_datetime < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
hint: Return staff full name and booking count.

q: What are the most common pickup locations?
sql: SELECT pickup_location, COUNT(*) FROM bookings GROUP BY pickup_location ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5
hint: Return pickup location and booking count for the top 5.

q: Which unicorns are reserved right now and for which customer?
sql: SELECT unicorn_name, current_customer FROM current_unicorn_availability WHERE status = 'reserved' ORDER BY unicorn_name
hint: Return unicorn name and customer name.

q: How many times has each unicorn gone into maintenance?
sql: SELECT u.name, COUNT(*) FROM unicorn_availability a JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = a.unicorn_id WHERE a.status = 'maintenance' GROUP BY u.name ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1
hint: Return unicorn name and number of maintenance events for every unicorn that had one.

q: What is the average booking duration in hours by breed?
sql: SELECT u.breed, ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (b.end_datetime - b.start_datetime)) / 3600)::numeric, 1) FROM bookings b JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id GROUP BY u.breed ORDER BY 2 DESC
hint: Return breed and average duration in hours rounded to 1 decimal.

q: How much booking-fee revenue did we collect per month in 2025?
sql: SELECT to_char(created_at, 'YYYY-MM'), SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'booking_fee' AND status = 'completed' AND created_at >= '2025-01-01' AND created_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
hint: Return year-month and summed booking-fee amount.

q: Which customers paid the most in booking fees in Q4 2025?
sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name, SUM(t.amount) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.transaction_type = 'booking_fee' AND t.created_at >= '2025-10-01' AND t.created_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10
hint: Return customer full name and amount for the top 10.

q: What is the average total cost of a booking?
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_cost), 2) FROM bookings
hint: Return one number rounded to 2 decimals.

q: Which cities do our customers come from, ranked by booking revenue?
sql: SELECT c.city, SUM(b.total_cost) FROM customers c JOIN bookings b ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY 2 DESC
hint: Return city and summed booking total cost.

q: How has our subscription price changed over time?
sql: SELECT datetime, plan_name, monthly_price FROM subscription_tracker_summary ORDER BY datetime
hint: Return each tracker record's timestamp, plan name and monthly price.

q: What percentage of our user limit are we using?
sql: SELECT user_limit_percent_used FROM account_subscription_status
hint: Return the user-limit percent used for each account.

q: Which unicorns with a longer-than-average horn earned the most?
sql: SELECT u.name, SUM(b.total_cost) FROM unicorns u JOIN bookings b ON b.unicorn_id = u.unicorn_id WHERE u.horn_length_cm > (SELECT AVG(horn_length_cm) FROM unicorns) GROUP BY u.name ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5
hint: Return unicorn name and summed booking total cost for the top 5.

q: What is the revenue per booked hour for each unicorn compared with its hourly rate?
sql: SELECT unicorn_name, hourly_rate, revenue_per_booked_hour FROM unicorn_performance_comparison ORDER BY revenue_per_booked_hour DESC
hint: Return unicorn name, hourly rate and revenue per booked hour for every unicorn.

q: How many bookings start in each hour of the day?
sql: SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM start_datetime) h, COUNT(*) FROM bookings GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
hint: Return the hour (0-23) and booking count.

q: For each breed, what is the average booking-fee amount?
sql: SELECT u.breed, ROUND(AVG(t.amount), 2) FROM transactions t JOIN bookings b ON b.booking_id = t.booking_id JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id WHERE t.transaction_type = 'booking_fee' GROUP BY u.breed
hint: Return breed and average amount rounded to 2 decimals.

q: Which clients booked the same unicorn more than three times?
sql: SELECT b.customer_id, u.name, COUNT(*) FROM bookings b JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id GROUP BY b.customer_id, u.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 ORDER BY 3 DESC
hint: Return customer id, unicorn name and count.

q: What was the reservation revenue by stable in December 2025?
sql: SELECT pickup_location, SUM(total_cost) FROM bookings WHERE start_datetime >= '2025-12-01' AND start_datetime < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY pickup_location ORDER BY 2 DESC
hint: Stable means pickup location. Return pickup location and summed booking total cost.

q: Which horses are overdue for servicing but still had rides booked in December 2025?
sql: SELECT DISTINCT u.name FROM unicorns u JOIN bookings b ON b.unicorn_id = u.unicorn_id WHERE u.next_service_due < CURRENT_DATE AND b.start_datetime >= '2025-12-01' AND b.start_datetime < '2026-01-01' ORDER BY u.name
hint: Horses means unicorns. Return the unicorn names only.

q: What is the daily rate revenue per customer account status?
sql: SELECT a.status, SUM(b.total_cost) FROM bookings b JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id = b.account_id GROUP BY a.status
hint: Use booking total cost. Return account status and summed total cost.

q: Which staff member took the most bookings from organization customers?
sql: SELECT u.first_name || ' ' || u.last_name, COUNT(*) FROM bookings b JOIN users u ON u.user_id = b.user_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type = 'organization' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Return the staff member's full name and booking count, 1 row.

q: Which 10 customers booked least often, and how much did each spend?
sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name, COUNT(*), SUM(b.total_cost) FROM bookings b JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, 1 ORDER BY 2, 3 LIMIT 10
hint: Return customer full name, booking count and summed total cost, 10 rows.

q: Compare utilization of unicorns that seat more than two riders with the rest.
sql: SELECT (u.seat_capacity > 2) big, ROUND(AVG(r.utilization_rate), 2) FROM unicorn_utilization_rates r JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = r.unicorn_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
hint: Return two rows: seats more than two (true/false) and average utilization rate rounded to 2 decimals.

q: Which customer departments spend the most, and on which breed?
sql: SELECT c.department, u.breed, SUM(b.total_cost) FROM customers c JOIN bookings b ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id WHERE c.department IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 10
hint: Return department, breed and summed booking total cost for the top 10 pairs.

q: What is the month-over-month growth in net revenue?
sql: SELECT year_month, net_revenue, ROUND(100.0 * (net_revenue - LAG(net_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year_month)) / NULLIF(LAG(net_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year_month), 0), 1) FROM monthly_revenue_summary ORDER BY year_month
hint: Return year-month, net revenue and percent change from the previous month rounded to 1 decimal.

q: How much time did each unicorn spend in maintenance versus being booked last month?
sql: SELECT unicorn_name, maintenance_hours, booked_hours FROM unicorn_utilization_rates ORDER BY maintenance_hours DESC
hint: Use the unicorn utilization view. Return unicorn name, maintenance hours and booked hours.

q: Which unicorns made of crystal horn earn above the average revenue per hour?
sql: SELECT p.unicorn_name FROM unicorn_performance_comparison p JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = p.unicorn_id WHERE u.horn_material ILIKE '%crystal%' AND p.revenue_per_booked_hour > (SELECT AVG(revenue_per_booked_hour) FROM unicorn_performance_comparison) ORDER BY 1
hint: Return the unicorn names only.

q: What is the gap between list hourly rate and the rate actually charged on bookings, by unicorn?
sql: SELECT u.name, u.hourly_rate, ROUND(AVG(b.base_hourly_rate), 2) FROM bookings b JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id GROUP BY u.name, u.hourly_rate ORDER BY u.hourly_rate - AVG(b.base_hourly_rate) DESC
hint: Return unicorn name, list hourly rate and average charged base rate rounded to 2 decimals.

q: Which customer segment has the highest average booking value?
sql: SELECT customer_segment FROM customer_segmentation_by_revenue ORDER BY avg_booking_value DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Return the segment name only.

q: What hour of the day has the most bookings on Saturdays and Sundays?
sql: SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM start_datetime) h FROM bookings WHERE EXTRACT(DOW FROM start_datetime) IN (0, 6) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Return the hour only.

q: Which unicorns bought for more than 10,000 have paid back their purchase price in booking revenue?
sql: SELECT u.name, u.purchase_price, SUM(b.total_cost) FROM unicorns u JOIN bookings b ON b.unicorn_id = u.unicorn_id WHERE u.purchase_price > 10000 GROUP BY u.name, u.purchase_price HAVING SUM(b.total_cost) >= u.purchase_price ORDER BY 3 DESC
hint: Return unicorn name, purchase price and summed booking total cost.

q: How many bookings did each staff member take for organization customers versus individuals?
sql: SELECT u.username, c.customer_type, COUNT(*) FROM bookings b JOIN users u ON u.user_id = b.user_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
hint: Return username, customer type and booking count.

q: Which month of 2025 had the most unique customers?
sql: SELECT year_month, unique_customers FROM monthly_revenue_summary ORDER BY unique_customers DESC LIMIT 1
hint: Return year-month and unique customer count, 1 row.

q: What is the average booking-fee amount for organization versus individual customers?
sql: SELECT c.customer_type, ROUND(AVG(t.amount), 2) FROM transactions t JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.transaction_type = 'booking_fee' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
hint: Return customer type and average amount rounded to 2 decimals.

q: Which bookings lasted more than 10 hours, and which unicorn was booked?
sql: SELECT b.booking_reference, u.name, ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (b.end_datetime - b.start_datetime)) / 3600, 1) hours FROM bookings b JOIN unicorns u ON u.unicorn_id = b.unicorn_id WHERE b.end_datetime - b.start_datetime > interval '10 hours' ORDER BY 3 DESC, 1 LIMIT 50
hint: Return booking reference, unicorn name and duration in hours rounded to 1 decimal, the 50 longest.
